user: I strongly prefer cruelty-free and vegan cosmetics products that have not been tested on animals.
assistant:  It's great to hear that you prefer cruelty-free and vegan cosmetics! Many people are becoming more conscious of the ethical implications of the products they use, including cosmetics, and are choosing to support companies that do not test on animals.

To ensure that the cosmetics you purchase are cruelty-free and vegan, you can look for certifications from organizations such as Leaping Bunny, PETA, or the Vegan Society. These organizations have strict standards for what constitutes cruelty-free and vegan, and companies must meet these standards in order to display their certifications.

Additionally, you can check the ingredient list of cosmetics products to ensure that they do not contain any animal-derived ingredients. Some common animal-derived ingredients to look out for include:

* Lanolin (derived from sheep's wool)
* Carmine (a red pigment derived from crushed insects)
* Guanine (a shimmery ingredient derived from fish scales)
* Beeswax (derived from bees)
* Collagen (derived from animal connective tissue)
